variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied to whatever the step shows: The held/not-held test is the finger opening in the scene at this decision step, not the cube line (the cube line may still report its old table position without a 'held' label while the cube is in fact held). 1. If the fingers are ~100% open (nothing held): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the current position of the goal-named cube as shown in the scene at this decision step (typically near [82, 127] at the start of execution). This is always the case at the first decision step. 2. If the fingers are ~46% open with the gripper raised (height around 0.15), the goal-named cube is held, regardless of whether the cube line carries a 'held' label or reports a stale table position (the execution steps just shown will show the fingers closing from 100% to ~46% at table height on the cube and not reopening): choose B, drop onto, pointing at goal_target from memory, which is already the target's execution-time position; the drop point is goal_target: look only for a target listed within a few pixels of goal_target in the scene at this decision step and point at that listed position, or at goal_target itself if no target is listed there at the moment (the list jitters under the passing gripper); every other target in the scene, however it shifts, vanishes or reappears between execution frames, is irrelevant and must never be chosen. If goal_target is unknown but demo_placements is non-empty, use the entry the goal ordinal selects (first=1, second=2, third=3, fourth=4) only if a target currently stands within a few pixels of it; otherwise fall to rule 4. 3. Never choose C (press the button); the button is part of the demonstration only, not of the task. 4. If the situation matches no rule (e.g. the cube is held but memory is empty and no list can be derived, or the cube is not visible): if a cube is held, drop onto the target nearest the image centre; otherwise choose A pointing at the goal-named cube's last visible position. After a drop has been completed the episode is over; if asked again, repeat rule 1 or 2 as the scene dictates.

fields.name: demo_placements
fields.description: At the first decision step (the one that shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS and the memory is empty), scan the demo frames for the cube whose colour the goal instruction names, and write the ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], where it was released: first find the STABLE target set: the four target positions listed in the demo frames where the goal-named cube is held raised and carried toward the image centre just before the final centre release (cube left near [82, 127]); every entry you write is one of those four positions, to the pixel. A release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper', and it counts only if it ends a real carry: frames labelled held with the gripper raised (height about 0.15) and the cube moving away from where it last rested, then the gripper lowered to table height and the fingers opening. A frame with fingers partly open (~39-46%) and the cube labelled held at table height on the very spot it already rested on, with no raised carry before it, is an artifact (it happens right after a button press, where the fingers were 0% open) and is NOT a placement; a grasp that lifts the cube and opens again on the very same target with no raised travel elsewhere in between is NOT a placement either. Every raised carry that ends with the cube resting within a few pixels of a stable target IS one placement, written in order, no matter what happens next: the cube being picked up again from that target later never removes the entry; the last placement is ALWAYS followed by such a re-grasp, because the demo ends by lifting the cube off its last target and carrying it to the centre, and that centre carry is the only carry you skip. Check before writing: entries = raised carries of the cube minus one, and at least the ordinal the goal names ('third' needs three entries). For each counted release decide by nearest match within a few pixels which stable target the cube now rests on, even if that target is missing from the release frame itself because the gripper hides it, and WRITE that target's position exactly as it is listed in the last demonstration frames before the final centre release (the frames just before the gripper carries the cube to about [82, 127] and opens). Never write values from the opening frames, from release frames, or from the final parked frames, even if they differ from the stable position by only a pixel or two; a target never gets two entries for one carry. Do NOT read target positions from the last demo frames: near the end of the demo, while the gripper is parked raised at about [54, 128], height 0.200, two targets may slide to new positions over a few frames (positions appear that match no earlier target) and the final frames show the shuffled layout. Skip the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127] with no target there), skip the cube's starting spot, and skip button presses (fingers 0% open, no cube held). At every later step, copy the carried-in value unchanged. Empty list if no demonstration frames are shown and nothing is carried in. e.g. releases on [107, 166], then [125, 119], then [97, 88], then a button press, a spurious 39%-open frame over [97, 88], then a re-grasp from [97, 88] into the centre carry: [[107, 166], [125, 119], [97, 88]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) was released during the DEMONSTRATION, in the order the releases happened. A release is a frame where the fingers go from ~46% open to ~100% open while that cube was 'held in the gripper' just before, and it produces an entry only when it ends a real carry: a run of frames in which the cube is labelled held with the gripper raised (height about 0.15) and the cube's position moves away from the spot where it last rested, followed by the gripper lowering to table height and the fingers opening. A frame with the fingers partly open (~39-46%) and the cube labelled held at table height on the very spot it already rested on, with no raised carry before it, is an artifact (typically right after a button press where the fingers were 0% open) and produces no entry; a grasp that lifts the cube and opens again on the very same target with no raised travel elsewhere in between produces no entry either. Every raised carry that ends with the cube resting within a few pixels of a target produces exactly one entry, no matter what happens afterwards: the cube being re-grasped off that target later (which always happens before the final centre carry, and may also happen before a carry to another target) never cancels the entry. Sanity check: the number of entries equals the number of raised carries of the cube minus one (the centre carry), and is at least the ordinal the goal names. The entry is the position of the target closest to the cube's resting spot right after the release, copied to the pixel from the STABLE pre-shuffle target set: the four target positions exactly as listed in the demonstration frames where the goal-named cube is held raised and carried toward the image centre just before the final centre release (cube left near [82, 127]). Every entry is one of those four positions, to the pixel, never a position read from a release frame, an opening frame or a parked frame, even if it differs by only a pixel or two. The opening frames, the release frames themselves and the final parked frames serve only to tell, by nearest match within a few pixels, which of the four stable targets received the cube; the value written is always the position from that pre-release list. Do NOT read positions from the last demo frames: while the gripper is parked raised at about [54, 128], height 0.200, at the end of the demonstration, two targets may slide to new positions over a few frames (positions appear that match no earlier target), usually swapping places, and the final frames show the shuffled layout. Match the cube's resting spot after the release against the stable set even if the target under the cube is missing from the release frame because the gripper hides it. Do NOT include the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127], no target there), do not include the cube's starting spot, do not include button presses, and do not include a release that is onto the same target the cube was just lifted from if no target lies under the cube. Written at step #1 (the only step that shows the demonstration) and copied unchanged at every later step. Empty list only if no demonstration was shown. e.g. releases on [107, 166], then [125, 119], then [97, 88], then a button press, a spurious 39%-open frame over [97, 88], then a re-grasp from [97, 88] into the centre carry: [[107, 166], [125, 119], [97, 88]]

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: At the first decision step, after writing demo_placements, take the entry of demo_placements the goal ordinal selects ('first' = entry 1, 'second' = entry 2, 'third' = entry 3, 'fourth' = entry 4). Then scan the parked frames at the end of the demonstration (gripper at about [54, 128], height 0.200, fingers 100% open, lasting many frames). Check each parked frame one at a time. Only if EVERY parked frame lists the same four positions as the stable set within a few pixels did nothing move: then write the target listed in the scene at the start of execution nearest the ordinal entry. If ANY single parked frame lists a position matching no stable target within a few pixels, the two stable targets absent from that frame are the movers, and they have swapped places, each ending at the other's original spot. Apply this even if the last parked frames and the scene at the start of execution again list four positions within a few pixels of the stable set: a swap ends with the movers on each other's old spots, so an unchanged-looking final layout is NOT evidence that nothing moved. If the ordinal entry is one of the movers, write the target listed in the scene at the start of execution nearest the OTHER mover's stable position; otherwise write the target nearest the ordinal entry. Do not track targets frame by frame through the parked frames. Write the position as listed in the execution scene, as a [y, x] point. This is the point to drop onto later. At every later step copy the carried-in value unchanged, to the pixel: a target drifting, disappearing or reappearing a few pixels away in execution frames because the gripper passes over it is never a reason to rewrite goal_target. unknown if demo_placements is empty. e.g. entry 3 is [143, 116]; one middle parked frame lists [113, 127] and [148, 85] and lacks [116, 101] and [143, 116], though the final frames look like the stable set again; the other mover is [116, 101]; the execution scene lists [116, 100]; goal_target = [116, 100]
fields.annotation: The position, in [y, x], AT THE START OF EXECUTION of the target that the goal instruction's ordinal picks out of demo_placements ('first' = entry 1, 'second' = entry 2, 'third' = entry 3, 'fourth' = entry 4), followed through the end-of-demonstration shuffle. Procedure: take the ordinal entry (its pre-shuffle position). Look at the parked frames at the end of the demonstration (gripper at about [54, 128], height 0.200, fingers 100% open). Take the parked frames one at a time. Only if EVERY parked frame lists the same four positions as the stable set (within a few pixels) did no target move: goal_target is then the target listed in the first execution frame nearest the ordinal entry. If ANY single parked frame lists a position that matches no stable target within a few pixels, the two stable targets absent from that frame are the movers and they exchange places, each ending where the other began. This holds even when the last parked frames and the first execution frame again list four positions within a few pixels of the stable set: a swap ends with the movers standing on each other's original spots, so an unchanged-looking final layout is not evidence that nothing moved. If the ordinal entry is one of the movers, goal_target is the target listed in the first execution frame nearest the OTHER mover's stable position; if it is not a mover, goal_target is the first execution frame's target nearest the ordinal entry. Do not track targets frame by frame through the parked frames; their paths cross and nearest-position tracking swaps the tracks. The value written is the position as listed in the first execution frame, to the pixel. Written at step #1 from the demonstration and copied unchanged afterwards. unknown before the demonstration has been seen. e.g. entry 3 is [143, 116]; one parked frame lists [113, 127] and [148, 85] and lacks [116, 101] and [143, 116], though the final frames list [116, 100] and [141, 117] again; the movers are [116, 101] and [143, 116]; the first execution frame lists [116, 100] nearest the other mover's stable spot; goal_target = [116, 100]

field demo_placements, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep this field, but change which frame the target positions are read from. The demonstration ends with the gripper parked raised at about [54, 128] height 0.200 for many frames; during those parked frames two of the four targets sometimes SLIDE to new positions over two or three frames (they appear at positions unlike any earlier target position, then settle), usually swapping places. So the last demo frame is NOT the frame to read target positions from. demo_placements stays the ordered chronological list, in [y, x], of the targets the goal-named cube was released on during the demonstration (release = fingers go from ~46% to ~100% after the cube was held; skip the final centre release near [82, 127], skip the starting spot, skip button presses), but each entry is the target's position read from the stable pre-shuffle target set: the four-target list seen in the frames before the final centre release and in the first parked frames afterwards, where all four positions still match the positions held throughout the demo. Match the cube's resting spot after the release against that pre-shuffle list even if the target under the cube is missing from the release frame itself (it is occluded by the gripper). Written at step #1, copied unchanged afterwards. e.g. [[137, 103], [115, 85]]

field goal_target, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  The position, in [y, x], at the START OF EXECUTION of the target that the goal instruction's ordinal picks out of demo_placements (first = entry 1, second = entry 2, ...), after following that target through the end-of-demo shuffle. Procedure: take the ordinal entry of demo_placements (pre-shuffle position). In the parked frames at the end of the demonstration, if the target list changes, track that target frame by frame: in each next frame it is the listed position nearest to its previous position among the positions that are not still occupied by an unmoved target; follow it until the list is stable again, and write its settled position, which equals one of the four target positions in the first execution frame. If no target moved, goal_target equals the demo_placements entry. Written at step #1 and copied unchanged afterwards; unknown before the demonstration is seen. Example: the first placement was on the target at [137, 103]; in the parked frames that target moved through [115, 110] and [98, 135] and settled at [101, 166], while the target from [101, 169] moved the other way to [137, 103]; goal_target = [101, 166].

In three episodes the policy chose B with the correct rule but the memory pointed at the wrong target because the end-of-demonstration target shuffle was not tracked; that is a memory fix (above), but rule 2 should state the dependency: point B at goal_target from memory, which is already the target's execution-time position, and confirm by choosing the target in the current scene nearest to goal_target (within a few pixels) and pointing at that listed position. Remove the fallback that applies the ordinal to demo_placements directly when goal_target is unknown: demo_placements holds pre-shuffle positions and the ordinal entry may no longer be where a target stands; if goal_target is unknown but demo_placements is non-empty, use the ordinal entry only if a target currently stands within a few pixels of it, otherwise fall to rule 4. Fingers ~100% open means nothing is held and rule 1 (A, point at the goal-named cube's current position) applies. Rule 3 (never press the button) stays.

refused
  Several reports at the just-grasped step said demo_placements must have been written in reverse order, mixed in releases of other cubes, counted the starting spot, or that 'second' maps onto the list differently; one said the first placement target was missing from the list. Reading the whole demonstrations, the lists were in correct chronological order and contained the right releases; the recorded drop points differ from the carried goal_target because two targets slid to new positions at the end of the demonstration, swapping places, so the target that received the ordinal placement now stands elsewhere. That is addressed by the shuffle-tracking change, not by reordering. One report asked the subgoal instruction to say not to trust goal_target when it conflicts with the ordinal applied to demo_placements; refused, since once goal_target is tracked through the shuffle it is goal_target that is right and the raw list entry that is stale.

fields.name: demo_placements
fields.description: At the first decision step (the one that shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS and the memory is empty), scan the demo frames for the cube whose colour the goal instruction names, and write the ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], where it was released: first find the STABLE target set: the four target positions listed in the demo frames where the goal-named cube is held raised and carried toward the image centre just before the final centre release (cube left near [82, 127]); every entry you write is one of those four positions, to the pixel. A release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper', and it counts only if it ends a real carry: frames labelled held with the gripper raised (height about 0.15) and the cube moving away from where it last rested, then the gripper lowered to table height and the fingers opening. A frame with fingers partly open (~39-46%) and the cube labelled held at table height on the very spot it already rested on, with no raised carry before it, is an artifact (it happens right after a button press, where the fingers were 0% open) and is NOT a placement; a re-grasp that lifts and sets the cube back on the same target without resting elsewhere is NOT a placement either. For each counted release decide by nearest match within a few pixels which stable target the cube now rests on, even if that target is missing from the release frame itself because the gripper hides it, and WRITE that target's position exactly as it is listed in the last demonstration frames before the final centre release (the frames just before the gripper carries the cube to about [82, 127] and opens). Never write values from the opening frames, from release frames, or from the final parked frames, even if they differ from the stable position by only a pixel or two; a target never gets two entries for one carry. Do NOT read target positions from the last demo frames: near the end of the demo, while the gripper is parked raised at about [54, 128], height 0.200, two targets may slide to new positions over a few frames (positions appear that match no earlier target) and the final frames show the shuffled layout. Skip the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127] with no target there), skip the cube's starting spot, and skip button presses (fingers 0% open, no cube held). At every later step, copy the carried-in value unchanged. Empty list if no demonstration frames are shown and nothing is carried in. e.g. releases on [107, 166], then [125, 119], then [97, 88], then a button press, a spurious 39%-open frame over [97, 88], then the centre carry: [[107, 166], [125, 119], [97, 88]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) was released during the DEMONSTRATION, in the order the releases happened. A release is a frame where the fingers go from ~46% open to ~100% open while that cube was 'held in the gripper' just before, and it produces an entry only when it ends a real carry: a run of frames in which the cube is labelled held with the gripper raised (height about 0.15) and the cube's position moves away from the spot where it last rested, followed by the gripper lowering to table height and the fingers opening. Do NOT include the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127], no target there), do not include the cube's starting spot, do not include button presses, and do not include a release that is onto the same target the cube was just lifted from if no target lies under the cube. Empty list only if no demonstration was shown. e.g. releases on [107, 166], then [125, 119], then [97, 88], then a button press, a spurious 39%-open frame over [97, 88], then the centre carry: [[107, 166], [125, 119], [97, 88]]
